findings.summary: The aggregation row mixes two ideas and gives a vague 'has-a' meaning that blurs it with composition.
findings.evidence: Aggregation also holds a reference, plus a whole-part grouping where the part lives on
findings.fix: Split into two bullets: 'Aggregation: whole-part, part outlives the whole' and drop the 'also holds a reference' clause, since association already covers references.

findings.summary: The 'Open arrowhead = navigable' bullet and 'A → B' bullet appear under a table that has no open-arrow row, so the notation is introduced without a visual and mixes with the three-lines idea.
findings.evidence: Open arrowhead = navigable: the source class can reach the target
findings.fix: Move navigability into its own short section with a small A → B diagram, separate from the three-lines table.

findings.summary: The 'Lifecycle Test' is shown as a flowchart and then repeated as a prose sentence, so the same content appears twice.
findings.evidence: Part outlives whole: aggregation. Part dies with whole: composition. Just a reference: association.
findings.fix: Remove the prose recap or replace it with a one-line mnemonic; keep the flowchart only.

findings.summary: The 'Dependency' arrow-direction bullet and the 'weak and temporary' bullet are separate ideas packed with examples, and the page states the dependency/association terms before the Strength Order diagram uses 'reference' as a label for association, which is inconsistent with 'uses / knows' on page 2.
findings.fix: Label the association step 'uses / knows' in the strength-order diagram to match page 2 and the cheat sheet.

findings.summary: The 'Roles and association classes' section holds several unrelated ideas (role names, where the role attribute is drawn, association class) in a bullet list and the Student–Course diagram is shown without any stated idea beforehand.
findings.evidence: The attribute implementing a role is shown on the line, not inside the box
findings.fix: Split roles and association classes into separate sections, and state the association-class idea in one line before the diagram.

findings.summary: The many-to-many diagram's multiplicities are inconsistent with the earlier diagram and its caption is ambiguous, making it hard to follow.

findings.summary: The multiplicity reading rule is stated in a way that contradicts the closing note and the worked example, so a skimmer may read it backwards.
findings.evidence: Read an end as: how many of that end's class per one instance of the other
findings.fix: Use one wording everywhere, e.g. 'The number next to a class says how many of that class link to one instance of the other class', and reuse it in the closing note and the cheat sheet.
